outcomes.text: Tell book-keeping from accounting.
State why a business measures its profit and loss.
Explain how accounting information helps monitor progress and make decisions.
Explain assets, liabilities and owner's equity.
Explain and apply the accounting equation.

topics.title: 2.1 The double entry system of book-keeping

outcomes.text: Outline how double entry book-keeping works.
Process accounting data using double entry.
Prepare ledger accounts and post transactions to them.
Balance ledger accounts and transfer balances to financial statements.
Interpret ledger accounts and their balances.
Recognise the sales, purchases and nominal ledgers.
Recognise and understand invoices, debit notes, credit notes, statements of account, cheques and receipts.
Complete pro-forma business documents.
Use business documents as sources of information, including counterfoils, paying-in slips and bank statements.

subtopics.title: Using the books of prime entry

outcomes.text: Explain the advantage of using different books of prime entry.
Process data in the cash book, petty cash book and journals.
Post ledger entries from the books of prime entry.

subtopics.title: Discounts, cash book and petty cash

outcomes.text: Tell trade discount from cash discount and account for each.
Explain the cash book as both a book of prime entry and a ledger account.
Record payments and receipts by bank transfer and other electronic means.
Explain and apply the imprest system of petty cash.
Explain that a trial balance lists ledger balances on a given date.
Outline the uses and limitations of a trial balance.
Prepare a trial balance and amend one containing errors.
Identify errors that do not affect the trial balance: commission, compensating, complete reversal, omission, original entry and principle.
Correct errors using journal entries.
Explain a suspense account as a temporary balancing measure.
Correct errors using suspense accounts.
Adjust profit or loss after correcting errors.
Explain the effect of correcting errors on the statement of financial position.
Explain the use and purpose of a bank statement.
Update the cash book for charges, interest, errors, credit transfers, direct debits, dividends and standing orders.
Prepare a bank reconciliation statement including bank errors, uncredited deposits and unpresented cheques.
Explain the purposes of purchases and sales ledger control accounts.
Identify the books of prime entry as sources for control account entries.
Prepare control accounts including credit transactions, discounts, returns, irrecoverable debts, dishonoured cheques, interest, contras and refunds.

topics.title: 4.1 Capital and revenue expenditure and receipts

subtopics.title: Capital and revenue expenditure and receipts

outcomes.text: Tell capital from revenue expenditure and account for each.
Tell capital from revenue receipts and account for each.
Calculate and comment on the effect of incorrect treatment on profit.
Calculate and comment on the effect of incorrect treatment on asset values.

topics.title: 4.2 Depreciation and disposal of non-current assets

outcomes.text: Define depreciation and explain why it is accounted for.
Describe the straight-line, reducing balance and revaluation methods.
Prepare ledger accounts and journals for the provision for depreciation.
Prepare ledger accounts and journals to record the sale of non-current assets, using disposal accounts.
Explain the importance of matching costs and revenues.
Record accrued and prepaid expenses in ledgers and journals.
Record accrued and prepaid incomes in ledgers and journals.

topics.title: 4.4 Irrecoverable debts and provision for doubtful debts

subtopics.title: Irrecoverable debts and provision for doubtful debts

outcomes.text: Explain irrecoverable debts and recovery of debts written off.
Record irrecoverable debts in ledgers and journals.
Record recovery of debts written off.
Explain why a provision for doubtful debts is kept.
Record the creation of, and changes to, a provision for doubtful debts.
Explain valuing inventory at the lower of cost and net realisable value.
Prepare simple inventory valuation statements.
Explain how an incorrect inventory valuation affects gross profit, profit, equity and assets.

Make the adjustments detailed for sole traders.

Make the adjustments detailed for sole traders.
